To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

repeated exposure to subconvulsive doses of trimethylolpropanephosphate (TMPP), a widely used flame retardant, induces central nervous system (CNS) sensitization and facilitates the induction of electrical kindling.

the administration of sub-convulsive dosages of trimethylolprobane phosphate, pentylenetrazol or FG-714-2, to rats induces a long term sensitization of the central nervous system that facilitates electrical kindling and may be associated with the development of chemical kindling.

repeated exposure to low doses of trimethylolproane phosphate, pentylenetrazole and FG-714, induces central nervous system (CNS) sensitization and facilitates the development of both chemical and electrical kindling in rats.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel animal model of epilepsy.
the development of an animal model that can be used to study the effects of environmental factors on the development of epilepsy.
the effects of repeated sub-convulsive administration of TMPP on seizure susceptibility.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TMPP, PT (pentylenetetra-zole), and FG (FG-7143) facilitate the development of electrical kindling and that this effect may be related to the development of chemical kindling.
the three compounds tested are not equally effective at facilitating electrical kindling.

TMPP, PT2 and FG-7143 are all capable of inducing central nervous system sensitisation, which is manifested by a decrease in the threshold and an increase in the duration of afterdischarges, and by a decrease in latency to the occurrence of after-discharges.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the repeated administration of TMPP, FG-7142 or PTZ induces a central nervous system sensitizing state that is associated with the facilitation of chemical and electrical kindling.
the three compounds are all effective in inducing chemical kindling and that TMPP and FG-7144 are both effective in facilitating electrical kindling.
TMPP is an effective convulsant, and that repeated exposure to subconvulsive doses of this agent induces a state of CNS sensitization that facilitates both chemical and electrical kindling.
The main takeaway from our work is that

repeated exposure to low doses of TMPP and other convulsants can sensitize the brain to the effects of subsequent convulsants, including electrical stimulation, and that such sensitization may play a role in the etiology of epilepsy.
the use of TMPP as a flame retardant should be discontinued because of the risk it poses to the central nervous system.
the repeated administration of sub-convulsive dosages of these compounds induces long term sensitization of the CNS.
